sermon.title: Two Reasons Sheep Go Astray
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: Pastor David G. Kincer explains that Jesus is the only Savior and the first reason sheep go astray: every one has turned to his own way, yet the Lord laid our iniquity on him. From Psalm 100 he invites all to know God and enter his gates with thanksgiving. From Matthew 18 he teaches that children are the greatest in the kingdom and warns against causing little ones or young believers to stumble.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: Points to check: “Zephaniah 3:17” cited for God rejoicing (wording unclear); three temple gates as spoken; the added “little” in Matthew 18:6 described as not in the Greek. Sensitive content kept as spoken: politicians and religionists saying all roads lead to God; public school teachers having sex with students “rampantly”; rejection of dispensationalism.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Now David was greatly distressed, for the people spoke of stoning him, because the soul of all the people was grieved, every man for his sons and his daughters. But David strengthened himself in the LORD his God.

faqs.question: Do all roads lead to the same God?
faqs.answer: No—besides the Lord there is no savior.

faqs.question: Whom can we blame for going our own way?
faqs.answer: No one but ourselves; we make the decision.

faqs.question: How important is music in church?
faqs.answer: Very—we come before his presence with singing.

faqs.question: Why use the name Jesus when witnessing?
faqs.answer: It makes people mad or glad; there’s no neutrality.

faqs.question: Do we have to wait for the next awakening?
faqs.answer: No—his truth can lead us into continual revival.

faqs.question: Should we speed-read the Bible?
faqs.answer: No—read it to know him and let him speak to you.

faqs.question: Who might cause little ones to stumble?
faqs.answer: Parents, relatives, teachers, friends or believers.

faqs.question: What is the church’s job toward young believers?
faqs.answer: To teach them, protect them and be an example.

faqs.question: Why be involved in a church?
faqs.answer: An individual is limited; a team can get a lot done.
